seo.title: The boom in €5 fast-food menus
seo.description: Find out what strategies fast-food chains use to attract customers in times of inflation.

fields.rt-blog-html:
Inflation and the rising cost of living are now top concerns for the French, who are looking for ways to save money without sacrificing the quality of their food. It is against this backdrop that we have seen a boom in 5-euro meal deals at fast-food restaurants. These offers, attractive due to their affordable prices, allow fast-food chains to build customer loyalty among those looking for good deals while staying competitive. Why are these low-cost meals so popular? How do these chains manage to offer such low prices? What are some concrete examples of this rapid growth?

‍

How do you explain the boom in 5-euro menus in fast-food restaurants?

Value for money

These anti-inflation menus offer consumers excellent value for money. For many customers—including students, families, and workers—these options make it possible to eat out without breaking the bank. Restaurants have recognized this and are offering complete meals at very competitive prices to prevent less affluent social classes from turning away from them.

Loyalty strategy

Offering discounted menus is also an effective strategy for attracting and retaining customers while maintaining its profit margin. During times of economic crisis and inflation, consumer loyalty is crucial for maintaining high foot traffic in restaurants. In this regard, €5 fast-food menus address this challenge by offering an affordable and appealing solution for quick meals.

Competitive response

With the rise of promotional offers and discounters, fast-food chains have to react if they are not to lose market share. 5-euro menus are a direct response to this competitive pressure.

👉 Learn more: Profit Margins in the Restaurant Industry: 6 Tips for Dealing with Inflation?

‍

How do fast-food restaurants manage to offer low-price formulas?

Cost optimization

Restaurants optimize their costs by streamlining their supply chain, negotiating favorable prices with their suppliers—particularly by purchasing in bulk—and standardizing their menus. This approach allows them to offer high-quality products at unbeatable prices. Digitalization also plays a key role: by adopting self-order kiosks to optimize costs in the fast-food industry, chains reduce checkout errors and speed up customer flow.

Limited offers

Many of these 5-euro meals are offered for a limited time or under certain conditions (off-peak hours, special promotions, etc.). This allows restaurants to manage their profit margins while creating a sense of urgency among consumers.

Simplified menus

These discount offers are often simplified, with a limited selection of products. In this way, fast-food outlets can cut costs while maintaining an attractive offer.

👉 To find out more: 5 tips to boost fast-food profitability

‍

What are some examples of anti-inflation measures?

1. McDonald's: not one, but 2 offers at €5 and €6

McDonald's stands out with its McFirst and McSmart menus, two complete and affordable meal options. The McFirst menu offers a choice of sandwiches (McFirst Chicken, McFirst Beef), a serving of fries or a small salad, and a medium drink for just 5 euros. The McSmart and McSmart+ menus, priced at 5 and 6 euros, offer two sandwiches, a serving of fries, and a drink—in small or medium sizes, depending on the option chosen.

2. KFC: the Megabox

Following the success of the Mega Menu and KFC’s Tuesday special, the fast-food chain recently introduced the KFC Mega Box. The concept is simple: a box containing five items, offered at a fixed price of €5.95 for a limited time. This allows customers to enjoy a complete, hearty meal at an affordable price.

3. Burger King: the cheap and tasty menu

Burger King's " Good and Inexpensive" Menu includes a burger, a serving of fries, a small drink, and a choice of onion rings, a small ice cream, or a coffee. Customers can choose from 5 different sandwiches: barbecue bacon, chicken, fish, double cheese, and a small goat cheese wrap. The small-size menu is priced at 5 euros, while the medium-size menu is 5.80 euros. For just 80 cents more, you can get a slightly larger portion of fries. With this offer, customers can enjoy the chain’s signature items at an unbeatable price.

4. Quick: a "Qarrément Bon" menu available for €5

Quick is also targeting this market with its "Qarrément Bon" menu for 5 euros, which includes a sandwich, a serving of fries, and a drink. It’s a simple and effective offer designed to attract fast-food lovers and bargain hunters.

5. Five Pizza: a special offer for €5.90 all year round

Five Pizza offers a year-round deal for 5.90 euros, which includes one pizza of your choice from a selection. It's an ideal option for pizza lovers on a budget.

6. Marie Blachère: P'tit Malin package for €5

The Marie Blachère bakery, in response to its competitors' special 'inflation' offers, is also proposing a tempting offer enabling its customers to choose 4 products from a pre-established selection (sandwiches, desserts, drinks), all for the modest sum of 5 euros. This initiative allows consumers to vary their pleasures at a lower cost.

7. O'Tacos: 4 for 5 €, O'Wow promotion

O'Tacos is teaming up with influencers Adem & Bilal for the launch of its O'Wow promotion. This campaign promotes a 5-euro deal that includes a triangle taco, two cheese rings, and a drink . The brand is thus boosting its appeal and attracting a young, tech-savvy customer base.

👉 Learn more: How do you set prices for your restaurant’s set menus?

The 5-euro menus are a smart response to current economic challenges. They are part of profitable business models in the fast-food industry that capitalize on high volume and customer loyalty. They allow consumers to eat at affordable prices while offering chains a way to build customer loyalty and stand out in a highly competitive market. The rapid rise of these low-cost, varied, and appealing meal options highlights the ability of fast-food chains to adapt to their customers’ expectations while constantly innovating.
